title: Scenario Sandbox with Confidence Bands for Batching & Cache Recommendations
creator: Aisha Kline
description: Create an interactive Scenario Sandbox inside the Redwood Console that lets operators and platform engineers compose workload profiles and immediately see recommended batching and cache policies with 'confidence bands' (median, p75, p95) for latency and cost. The UI should surface explainers for each recommendation, highlight guardrail violations (e.g., latency SLO breach, data isolation constraints), and allow snapshotting/exporting presets to rollouts. Focus on a lightweight prototype (Figma + clickable) and a small simulation harness that uses historical telemetry + synthetic tails to estimate variance.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype of the Scenario Sandbox flows (editor, policy recommender, results panel) approved by PM and eng
Confidence-band visualization implemented in prototype with toggle between latency and cost metrics
Explainability pane for each recommendation with short rationale and links to model-level trade-offs
Guardrail layer shows clear warnings and suggested automatic fallback policies
Prototype run-through & moderated usability test with 5 engineers (notes captured)
Export button that creates a named preset (JSON) that can be consumed by rollout service
design_notes: Sandbox sits as a modal overlay from the model route and also accessible from per-route optimization card
Simulation engine will accept a sample distribution (qps, avg_tokens, prefix_share) and run a fast approximation using historic trace aggregates
Confidence bands computed by bootstrap over recent traces + synthetic tail stretch to approximate p95 with limited data
Results panel shows three rows (latency, cost, cache-hit) each with median/p75/p95 bands; use monochrome gradients with accent color for warnings
Explainability microcopy: two-line rationale + 'what changed' diff (e.g., +12% cache hit with small prefix increase)
Accessible tooltips: include short examples of when a recommendation is conservative vs aggressive
Include small 'impact map' that ties settings to unit economics (cost/token) and to route-level SLA impact
decisions: Use three statistical bands (median, p75, p95) instead of mean+stddev for skewed token/time distributions
Default preset = 'Conservative' (prioritizes latency SLO); users can switch to 'Balanced' or 'Aggressive'
Snapshots auto-save to user workspace and are exportable as a rollout preset for canary deployments
Prototype will use anonymized bucketed traces to avoid PII and keep simulation fast
tradeoffs: High-fidelity simulation requires more telemetry and compute; we'll start with a fast approximation and flag uncertainty
More features in-sandbox increases cognitive load; we keep primary screen minimal and move advanced knobs to an 'Advanced' accordion
Auto-suggested policies are opinionated — risk of overreach; include clear opt-out and explanation to maintain trust
